title: Managed surge crediting and grace-window orchestration
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem statement: Customers using Dedicated fleets occasionally experience short, high-intensity traffic spikes (1–20 minutes) that exceed their reserved throughput. Today we either (a) deny excess requests during the spike or (b) allow them and invoice full overage immediately. Both approaches create bad UX: dropped requests for critical user flows or surprise invoices that break trust. We need a controlled way to offer brief extra capacity while preserving fair scheduling across tenants and producing predictable, auditable billing.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Implement a configurable "grace window" per customer (default 10 minutes) that allows soft over-provisioning without immediate hard overage invoicing. 2) Introduce a per-tenant "surge credit ledger" that tracks temporary capacity consumed and amortizes charges across the next billing period according to a policy. 3) Autoscaler and router must respect soft-fence limits: when grace window is active, scheduler may borrow from a shared surge pool with priority-adjusted allocation. 4) Console shows timeline of grace window usage, ledger entries, and projected invoice impact. 5) Operator runbook for manual reconciliation and emergency revocation is available.
design_summary: High-level approach: create a new 'surge mediation' layer between the fleet router and the autoscaling allocator. Components: (a) Surge Pool Controller: maintains a global reservoir of ephemeral capacity tokens funded by pre-reserved headroom and operator-assigned spare nodes. (b) Tenant Surge Ledger: lightweight per-tenant ledger (time-series entries) recording tokens consumed, start/end of grace windows, and amortization metadata. (c) Grace Window Manager: policy engine implementing duration, max tokens, and backstop behaviour (automatic rollover to overage billing after recovery window). (d) Billing Smoother: periodic job that computes prorated charges and converts ledger entries to invoiceable line items with tags for operator adjustments. Interaction patterns: requests exceeding tenant reserved QPS consult Surge Pool Controller. If tokens available and tenant within per-window limits, tokens are consumed and request is admitted with metadata in the trace for audit. If no tokens or tenant hit hard cap, fallback policies apply (retry, queue, or throttle).
implementation_notes: - Autoscaler changes: expose a short-lived 'temporary_quota' API for the allocator to grant or revoke capacity without altering the tenant's persistent reservation. - Router changes: attach surge metadata to traces and export to Console for visualization. - Billing changes: ledger stored in Timescale and mirrored to Billing pipeline with a tenant-facing explanation field. - Operator tools: add UI to view active grace windows, force-revoke tokens, and mark ledger entries as 'waived' or 'disputed'. - Safety: hard global cap to prevent surge pool depletion; dynamic backpressure to protect SLOs for high-priority tenants. - Data retention: ledger entries retained 90 days for audit and 13 months for invoicing disputes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary, internal tenants): enable grace-window off by default; run for 2 weeks with internal tenants and monitor latency, error-rate, and surge pool utilization. Phase 2 (opt-in customers): enable for customers with dedicated fleets who opt in and accept tentative billing smoothing. Phase 3 (default opt-in for new tenants): enable by default with conservative limits. Monitoring: surge_pool_utilization, per-tenant_grace_window_count, amortized_charge_projection, disputed_ledger_percentage. KPI thresholds for rollback: >2% spike in 95th pct latency across dedicated fleets, or >5% of surge charges disputed within 7 days.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Surge pool starvation could allow a noisy tenant to exhaust spare capacity. Mitigation: introduce per-tenant dynamic soft cap based on historical usage and priority class. Risk: Accounting complexity could delay invoicing. Mitigation: run Billing Smoother in a read-only dry-run mode for 2 billing cycles to validate outputs. Risk: Regulatory concerns about deferred billing. Mitigation: create opt-out and explicit consent flows and include clear ledger entries in invoices.

2025-06-18 — Prototype results: canary with 5 internal tenants showed surge_pool_utilization peaking at 42% with no measurable increase in P95 latency. Found race on token revocation path — added compare-and-swap to Surge Pool Controller.
2025-06-21 — Security review kickoff: noted that ledger entries include tenant-id and cost tags; we flagged retention and RBAC controls for SRE and Compliance to review.
